videos.title: They Slept for 309 Years
videos.topic: The People of the Cave (Surah Al-Kahf)
videos.hook: A group of young men fell asleep in a cave, and woke up three hundred years later.
videos.script: A group of young men fell asleep in a cave, and woke up three hundred years later. This is not a legend someone invented. It is in the Quran, in Surah Al-Kahf. They were young believers living in a city that worshipped idols. To protect their faith, they fled into a cave and begged their Lord for mercy. And Allah sealed their ears in a deep sleep. The Quran describes the scene in detail. When the sun rose, it turned away from their cave. When it set, it passed them by. Anyone who looked at them would think they were awake. Their bodies were turned from side to side, while their dog lay stretched out at the entrance. When they finally woke, they thought they had slept a day, or part of a day. One of them went into the city with a silver coin, into a world that had moved on without them. The Quran says they stayed three hundred years, and added nine. Some scholars have noticed that three hundred solar years is almost exactly three hundred and nine lunar years. Three centuries passed outside. Inside the cave, it felt like a single day.
videos.accuracy_note: Quran, Surah Al-Kahf 18:9-26 (the flight, the sleep, the sun turning away, the dog, the silver coin, '300 years and added nine'). The solar/lunar-year observation (300 solar years = about 309 lunar years) is a later scholarly observation, labeled as such in the script.
videos.caption: They closed their eyes for one night... and opened them three centuries later. Did you know this story is in the Quran?
videos.continuity: Seven-ish young believers in plain undyed wool robes and simple head cloths; a slender sand-colored dog; a rocky mountain cave above an ancient walled city of temples and statues; warm golden light versus deep blue shadow.

videos.title: The Angel Who Filled the Sky
videos.hook: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saw the angel Jibril in his true form only twice.
videos.script: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saw the angel Jibril in his true form only twice. And both times, he filled the horizon. Most of the time, Jibril came in the form of a man. The companions once saw him like this: a stranger in brilliant white clothes, with no trace of travel on him, who sat before the Prophet and asked about Islam. But his real form was something else. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud reports that the Prophet saw Jibril with six hundred wings. And in Sahih Muslim, Aisha reports the Prophet's own words. He saw Jibril descending from the sky, and the greatness of his form filled everything between heaven and earth. The Quran points to these moments: 'And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon.' And again, at the Lote Tree of the utmost boundary. Think about that. The angel who brought the Quran down to earth was so vast he could cover the sky. And yet the message he carried was made for one small human heart. Yours.
videos.accuracy_note: Authentic hadith: Sahih al-Bukhari 4856-4857 (Ibn Mas'ud: Jibril with six hundred wings); Sahih Muslim 177 (Aisha: the Prophet saw Jibril in his created form only twice, his greatness filling what is between heaven and earth); Sahih Muslim 8 (the hadith of Jibril in human form). Quran 81:23 and 53:13-14.
videos.caption: Six hundred wings. A form that filled the space between heaven and earth. This is how the Prophet described Jibril.
videos.continuity: Angels appear only as radiant white-gold light and luminous wings, never with faces. Setting: the desert mountains around Mecca, Mount Hira, and the simple palm-trunk mosque of Medina.

videos.title: The Prayer From Inside the Whale
videos.hook: There are words that were spoken from inside the belly of a whale, and the Prophet said they are still answered today.
videos.script: There are words that were spoken from inside the belly of a whale, and the Prophet said they are still answered today. Prophet Yunus was sent to a city that refused to listen. He left them in anger, and boarded a heavily loaded ship. Out at sea, the ship was in danger. They cast lots, and the lot fell on Yunus. He was thrown into the dark water, and a great fish swallowed him. The Quran says he called out from within the darknesses. Early scholars explained them as three: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness inside the whale. And from there, he said: 'There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Truly, I have been among the wrongdoers.' Allah answered him. The fish cast him onto the shore, weak and sick, and a gourd plant grew over him. The Quran says that if he had not glorified Allah, he would have stayed in that belly until the Day of Resurrection. And the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said that no Muslim makes this prayer for anything, except that Allah answers him. Right after this story, Allah says: 'And thus do We save the believers.' Whatever darkness you are in tonight, you now know the words.
videos.accuracy_note: Quran 21:87-88 (the call from within the darknesses, 'thus do We save the believers'), 37:139-148 (the laden ship, the lots, the fish, the shore, the gourd plant, 'until the Day they are resurrected'). Hadith: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3505 (no Muslim makes this supplication except that Allah answers him; graded sahih by al-Hakim and al-Albani). The 'three darknesses' explanation comes from early commentators (Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, in Tafsir Ibn Kathir) and is labeled as such.
videos.caption: He was in the darkest place on earth, and he said one sentence. Save these words.
videos.continuity: Prophet Yunus is never shown: his presence is implied through the ship, the sea, the whale, light, and the shore. Ancient Nineveh on a river; a wooden merchant ship; a colossal dark whale; a sandy shore with broad green gourd leaves.
